title.rendered: Morgan survives the showers for first Cataclean Plato Racing victory

excerpt.rendered: Cataclean Plato Racing's Adam Morgan took the chequered flag in...

content.rendered:
Cataclean Plato Racing's Adam Morgan took the chequered flag in Round 16 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Knockhill, taking the team's first triumph whilst leading a one-two ahead of teammate Daniel Rowbottom.

The success is testament to the hard work put in by the rookie squad and in particular the progress made with the Mercedes A35 Saloons since the mid-summer break.

A first podium for the outfit at Thruxton last time out has been followed up by Morgan's 'Race to Pole' win in Scotland yesterday and the team's first proper win in today's opener.

Morgan had to deal with very wet conditions and a late race safety car, but the Lancashire driver was always in control of the contest, as Rowbottom played rear gunner in the closing laps.

Rowbottom had earlier relinquished Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden of second with an impressive move, whilst the Scotsman then had to turn his attentions to his rear mirrors.

Incredibly, there were a cool nine Drivers' titles between the racers battling for third at the finish, as Shedden saw off the challenges from the title chasing duo of Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU).

Sutton had got the better of Ingram in the earlier running with the former charging up through the order from 11th on the grid.

Some stellar moves amidst extreme conditions looked to be heading towards yet another rostrum for the #116 Ford Focus Titanium, but when Ingram's #80 Hyundai i30N gradually shadowed him then attention turned to keeping his old adversary behind.

Ricky Collard (Team VERTU) was sixth ahead of a trio of Audi A3 Saloons, led by the feisty Scotsman Dexter Patterson. Mikey Doble was next in the order, whilst another local man – Aiden Moffat – stormed from the back of the grid to take ninth.

NAPA Racing UK's Sam Osborne rounded out the top ten.

title.rendered: Sutton seals seventh success in Scotland

excerpt.rendered: NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton surged to victory in Round...

content.rendered:
NAPA Racing UK's Ash Sutton surged to victory in Round 17 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Knockhill, to take his seventh race win of the campaign and extend his advantage at the top of the standings.

Starting from fourth on the grid, Sutton made light work of Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) and Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing) ahead of him before he set about attacking Daniel Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing) for the lead.

There was disappointment behind for Sutton's main title rival – Team VERTU's Tom Ingram – already nursing a power problem off the line before he was soon forced into retirement following contact. As the action concertinaed ahead of him, the #80 Hyundai went into the back of Shedden's Toyota on the run to the chicane for the first time, and immediately had to pit with radiator damage.

Local favourite Aiden Moffat was another early casualty when his LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi was caught up in a separate incident.

Rowbottom performed extremely well in the #32 Mercedes A35 Saloon out front, particularly considering the lack of boost available while also running the harder Goodyear tyre compound.

There was little Rowbottom could do to stop his former teammate however, as Sutton's #116 Ford Focus Titanium sliced down the inside at the final hairpin.

Two safety car periods interrupted proceedings with the second delay only allowing for a final one-lap shootout at the finish.

Sutton's cruised home while Rowbottom fended off Team VERTU's Ricky Collard, who again continues his standout BTCC season in style.

Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) and Charles Rainford (WSR) starred in fourth and sixth respectively with the latter bursting through from 21st on the grid following his difficult opening race this morning.

Morgan ensured that it was another double celebration for Cataclean Plato Racing with a top five finish, again running on the harder tyre and with minimal boost.

Three-time champion Shedden hung on to seventh ahead of fellow countryman Dexter Patterson in the #17 Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing Audi.

A trio of NAPA Racing UK cars followed in the order with Dan Cammish, Sam Osborne and Lewis Selby finishing in ninth, tenth and eleventh respectively.

content.rendered:
Team VERTU's Tom Chilton took the chequered flag in Round 18 of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, taking his 19th career BTCC triumph and the third of his career at Knockhill.

The experienced tin top star has endured a mixed 2026 campaign so far with a solitary podium at Snetterton being a high point, but those misfortunes are now a thing of the past as the #3 Hyundai driver dominated the finale in Scotland.

If Chilton was pleased with his pillar-to-post triumph then Adam Morgan was overjoyed with his weekend's work as he ended the day with a second place, following on from his 'Race to Pole' win, race one victory and another top five finish – comfortably the Cataclean Plato Racing driver's best weekend of the season.

The podium was completed by the battling Dan Cammish as the multiple race winner closed in on Tom Ingram in the overall standings.

Dexter Patterson was another to round off a fantastic weekend at his home circuit as the Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing driver claimed fourth and with it the Jack Sears Trophy honours, following two top eight results earlier in the day.

The WSR duo of Charles Rainford and Daryl De Leon finished proceedings north of the border in solid style with fifth and sixth respectively, whilst Dan Rowbottom completed a great weekend for Cataclean Plato Racing with seventh.

Speedworks Corolla Racing's Josh Cook was eighth while Team VERTU teammates – Ricky Collard and Tom Ingram – completed the top ten positions.

The BTCC will be back in action in two weeks' time at Donington Park.

Sutton is closing in on a potential record-breaking fifth overall drivers’ title and left the tight, twisty circuit with a firm grip on proceedings, while second-placed Tom Ingram lost ground to Dan Cammish.

Four-time champ Sutton holds an 81-point lead at the top of the order, whilst Cammish has closed to within 13 points of second placed Ingram.

Alliance Racing/Ford and its NAPA Racing UK outfit retain a commanding advantage at the top of both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ standings, while Mikey Doble and LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing remain in control of the Independents’ honours.

Dexter Patterson also enjoyed a standout weekend, pulling clear of James Dorlin in the race for the Jack Sears Trophy.

The BTCC returns to action in two weeks’ time, on 22/23 August, at Donington Park.

NAPA Racing UK's Sutton surged to victory in Round 17, to take his seventh race win of the campaign and extend his advantage at the top of the standings.

I’ve been doing this for a long time so just to get a pole position was amazing but to top it off with a win and a second is just mind-blowing. It’s a huge credit to the team, the sponsors and everybody involved – a huge thank you.”

title.rendered: Moffat leads Scottish one-two at Knockhill

excerpt.rendered: There was double joy for both Scotland and Power Maxed...

content.rendered:
There was double joy for both Scotland and Power Maxed Racing in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Practice Session at Knockhill as Aiden Moffat led home Audi stablemate Dexter Patterson at the top of the timesheets.

The fast and frenetic 50-minute session saw all 23 cars take to the track with hundreds of miles completed around the undulating Fife circuit.

Times improved rapidly as the session wore on with the EXCELR8 Motorsport duo of Tom Ingram and Ricky Collard both enjoying brief spells at the top, whilst the Cataclean Plato Racing duo of Dan Rowbottom and Adam Morgan held a one-two of their own in the closing 15 minutes, as the Mercedes-run squad continue to show improved performance.

It was the Audi PMR outfit that kept its powder dry until the final ten minutes as Moffat, Patterson and Doble all fired in fantastic times.

LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing’s Moffat earned the final bragging rights as his 50.840s lap time dipped under Ash Sutton’s race lap record from 2020, whilst Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing’s Patterson ended up just 0.080s off the benchmark.

Rowbottom secured third ahead of Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing), whilst Morgan completed an-all Audi-Mercedes top five.

Impressively, Chris Smiley was the best of the rest in the Restart Racing Hyundai, ahead of reigning champion Ingram in the same i30N machine.

Daryl De Leon (WSR), Aron Taylor-Smith (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) and Collard (EXCELR8 Motorsport) completed the top ten positions.

As a reminder, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter 17 lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

title.rendered: Morgan masters Knockhill to win 'Race to Pole'

excerpt.rendered: Cataclean Plato Racing's Adam Morgan claimed his first Kwik Fit...

content.rendered:
Cataclean Plato Racing's Adam Morgan claimed his first Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship pole position since 2018 after winning today's (8 August) Qualifying Race at Knockhill.

Mercedes man Morgan showed the upturn in pace for the rookie outfit with his second overall career pole in Britain's elite motorsport championship, whilst teammate Dan Rowbottom confirmed the squad's speed with third at the finish.

There was local joy too as Gordon Shedden's Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport Toyota was sandwiched between the two 'Silver Arrows' at the conclusion of the 20-lap race.

It was almost a one-two for Cataclean Plato Racing with Rowbottom running side-by-side with Shedden across the start/finish line for the penultimate time, but the three time champion used his quality and experience to hold off his rival.

There was drama on the opening tour when Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing) and Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing) were both fired off track in separate incidents, the latter involving a heavy hit into the barrier for his Toyota at the chicane.

The top three positions remained settled following the restart but there was a quick change behind as Chris Smiley (Restart Racing) scythed by Charles Rainford's WSR BMW for fourth at the final hairpin.

The WSR pairing of Rainford and Daryl De Leon eventually had to settle for fifth and sixth, as the 330i M Sports showed good consistency rather than race-winning pace, whilst the fight for seventh kicked off behind.

It was Mikey Doble that won that particular battle as he got the draft out of the final hairpin on the last lap. The #88 Audi A3 Saloon ran side-by-side with Ricky Collard's Team VERTU Hyundai across the line and incredibly took the place by just 0.006s, whilst reigning champion Tom Ingram (Team VERTU) looked on from behind.

Dan Cammish resisted the pressure from NAPA Racing UK teammate Ash Sutton to take a top ten finish, with the Ford Focus Titanium duo separated by less than half a second.

Full credit, however, went to Morgan as he not only claimed his first qualifying success for eight years, but he also secured the second 'Race to Pole' triumph for Cataclean Plato Racing. The Cheshire driver had finished either sixth or seventh in the previous Qualifying Races so far this season so today's performance represented a huge turnaround for the multiple race winner.

Rounds 16, 17 and 18 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at Knockhill tomorrow with the action getting underway in the UK on ITV4 from 11:15. The races will also be beamed around the world on Racer TV (North America) and the BTCC YouTube Channel (Rest of the World).

Adam Morgan, Cataclean Plato Racing, said: "It's mega. The car is in a lovely spot here. It's allowing you to use the kerbs, it's got really good traction and I've just been able to really get on top of it. My first pole position was back at Rockingham in 2018, so we've had to wait a while, but we've finally done it. It's a great start to the weekend for Dan (Rowbottom) and I and we can hopefully keep moving forward. I think we're in a good place. We're back!"

title.rendered: Team VERTU Targets Top Step in Scotland

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU will look to add to an impressive record...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU will look to add to an impressive record of success at Knockhill when the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship makes the annual visit to Scotland this weekend for the sixth event of the season.

The EXCELR8-run team crosses the border seeking to strengthen its title challenge, with defending champion Tom Ingram currently sitting second in the Drivers’ standings and Team VERTU having moved into the same position in the Teams’ Championship following the previous meeting at Thruxton.

Ingram fought his way to a second victory of the year last time out in Hampshire but finds himself playing catch-up to long-time rival Ash Sutton in the standings at the halfway stage of the season.

The two-time champion’s record at Knockhill includes an impressive victory last season, the largest winning margin seen that year, whilst he has picked up a total of seven podium finishes at the Fife venue.

Ricky Collard remains the second-highest Team VERTU driver in the standings having moved up to fifth spot at Thruxton, where he battled back from a retirement in the Qualifying Race to bag a best finish of fourth.

The former British GT Champion is seeking to add to an impressive record of five podium finishes already this year – more than doubling his career tally through the first half of the season.

Like Ingram, Tom Chilton is a multiple winner at Knockhill through the years, having made his first outing at the circuit back in 2002.

Chilton rebounded well to pick up three points finishes in Hampshire after a troublesome Qualifying Race of his own, but has so far managed just a single podium finish this year to sit 13th in the standings.

Nicolas Hamilton enjoyed another productive weekend at Thruxton as he secured points for the fourth successive event, meaning he has already surpassed his previous best for points scored in a season.

Hamilton also moved up into third place in the Jack Sears Trophy and makes the trip to Scotland with confidence on a high at a circuit he admits is one of his favourites on the calendar.

Three solid finishes remain his first target for the weekend to maintain the impressive progress he has made since joining the team at the start of the season, with the ultimate goal being to extend his points-scoring run.

Saturday’s qualifying session and qualifying race are scheduled to take place from 14:00 and will air live on YouTube, with the three races on Sunday being aired live on ITV4 at 11:15, 14:15 and 17:20.

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “The issues we had in the qualifying race at Thruxton really hampered our chances on race day but we battled back well to get up into the top ten – although that’s not where I was hoping to be.

“Heading to Knockhill, I’m hoping for a more trouble-free weekend which will allow us to really make the most of the pace we have in the car. Last season we managed to come from the back of the grid to take a pair of top eight finishes so if we can qualify well, there is no reason why we can’t expect to be near the front.

“Knockhill is a circuit that I have always enjoyed and where I’ve scored silverware in the past. The target is to try and add to that this weekend.”

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “On my last visit to Knockhill in 2023, I picked up a podium finish and had my best weekend of the season, and I also won there whilst competing in British F4, so there are plenty of fond memories from earlier in my career.

“Heading back to Scotland this time around, I’m feeling confident about my chances of another strong performance to build on what has been a really positive season so far.

“The Hyundai is a proven race winner at Knockhill and having missed out on a podium at Thruxton, my target is to get back into the top three and battle for some trophies.”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton was one of the events I was least looking forward to and I managed to come away with some points, which leaves me confident going to Knockhill – which is a circuit I love.

“The Scottish crowd is great and the track is amazing; it’s like being on a giant rollercoaster where you’re constantly on two wheels and there is always something going on.

“Obviously I’ve not driven the Hyundai there before as has been the case with most of the circuits that we’ve visited, but I’m confident that we are going to have a strong package and I’m really excited to see what we can achieve in terms of results.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton was a stronger weekend for us than the results on paper suggest, even with the victory in the final race, and we now head for Knockhill hoping to build on the positive results we have gained there in the past.

“Going into the second half of the season, we know there is a huge challenge ahead of us as we look to close the gap at the top of the standings but the whole team is focused on going the best job we can do over the remaining five rounds.

“Track position is key at Knockhill so it’s going to be important to try and maximise our performance during Saturday to ensure that we are towards the sharp end of the grid when it comes to Sunday’s three races.

“I’ve been around the BTCC long enough to know how quickly things can change and one difficult weekend can have a big impact – as I’ve seen personally this year already. With that in mind, we’ve got to push hard to ensure that we pick up as many points as possible this weekend to strengthen our position.”

title.rendered: Driven by Sport welcomes families to Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: The new-for-2026 community initiative, Driven by Sport presented by Kwik...

content.rendered:
The new-for-2026 community initiative, Driven by Sport presented by Kwik Fit, continued its successful inaugural year with an engaging and inspiring event at Thruxton Circuit last month.

Held in the school holidays for the first time, the event offered a fresh BTCC-inspired experience, with local children attending alongside their parents and a number of competition winners securing places through the BTCC website and social media channels.

Guests once again enjoyed a broad range of STEM-led and interactive activities, each offering an engaging insight into the many roles and career opportunities available across motorsport.

These included engineering, first aid, car design, tyre technology, television presenting and, of course, the ever-popular sim racing experience. Furthermore, it wasn’t just the kids joining in with the fun this time around as the parents took on the challenges too, making for an unforgettable family experience for those in attendance.

Attendees also had the opportunity to meet BTCC driver Dan Rowbottom, get close to the championship’s racing cars and enjoy a behind-the-scenes look at life inside the BTCC paddock. In particular, guests got to speak to Power Maxed Racing driver Mikey Doble and his team in their garage, with the opportunity to apply ‘Driven by Sport’ stickers to one of the cars seen across the world all weekend.

The hands-on career discovery programme for school-age students combines education and entertainment through immersive, motorsport-themed experiences delivered by industry professionals, showcasing the many pathways into the sport.

The Thruxton event formed part of a growing programme of community-focused activities organised by the BTCC, including school and hospital visits, charitable events and further Driven by Sport experiences.

By welcoming parents and the wider BTCC community on this occasion, the programme – presented by BTCC Title Partner Kwik Fit – was able to introduce an even broader audience to the diverse skills and careers that contribute to the success of the championship.

excerpt.rendered: WSR anticipate raucous local support this weekend for local driver...

content.rendered:
WSR anticipate raucous local support this weekend for local driver Lewis Gilbert as the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship ventures north of the border for its annual Scottish event at Knockhill.

The triple-header race weekend at the Fife circuit marks the beginning of the second half of the season for the UK’s most popular racing series and gives the 18-time champions a great opportunity to add to their two wins so far in 2026.

Scottish rookie Gilbert, who is joined by team-mates Charles Rainford and Dary De Leon, is excited for what is only his second BTCC event; the Dalry, North Ayrshire, driver having switched to touring cars from single-seaters less than a month ago.

The 22-year-old came close to scoring points on his BTCC debut last time out at Thruxton and is eager to make good on his promise in front of his home crowd aboard his BMW 330i M Sport.

Team-mates Rainford and De Leon are both eager to return to the podium after enduring frustrating weekends at Thruxton last time out.

The former has won twice in 2026 aboard his BMW 330i M Sport – those victories coming at Snetterton and Oulton Park ahead of the summer break – and the Horsham racer is determined to achieve more success in Scotland.

Rainford headed an all-WSR top three to score his first career BTCC pole position at the 1.3-mile circuit last year, adding a second-place finish and setting the fastest race lap of the event.

De Leon, meanwhile, started second – his maiden front-row qualifying result – and scored valuable Jack Sears Trophy points during a campaign in which he would eventually become class champion.

The Anglo-Filipino, who turned 21 this week, was a double podium-finisher at Snetterton and is currently second in the Independent Drivers’ points

WSR have the best record of any current BTCC team at Knockhill with 19 race wins, including double victories in each of the past three seasons, and pole positions in four of the past five visits to the track.

Lewis Gilbert (#29): “It’s pretty cool that in only my second event in the BTCC, I have the chance to race at my home track. Knockhill’s about an hour away from where I live so it’s as local as it gets for me. Although I’ve never raced there, I’ve done a rally and I’ve driven the circuit on track days so I’m familiar with the layout and it’s a pretty testing one for just over a mile. I’ve watched BTCC at Knockhill before there and always noticed how great the support is for Scottish drivers, so hopefully we can get some good results to really get the crowd cheering.”

Charles Rainford (#99): “I can’t wait to get to Knockhill and to the scene of my first BTCC pole position last year. After the challenging time we had at Thruxton, I’ll be very glad to be back a tight and twisty track that should suit our BMWs down to the ground. Last year it was podiums and fastest laps for me in Scotland, but this time I’m determined to get that big ‘Number One’ board and come away with a win.”

Daryl De Leon (#2): “Going from Thruxton to Knockhill is pretty much the biggest change you can get in the BTCC – the two tracks are the total opposite. I don’t mind that, though, as Knockhill should be really good for our BMWs. The rear-wheel-drive layout means we can put the power down really well out of the hairpin and get a good slingshot up the straight. After qualifying on the front row last year, I’m setting my targets nice and high.”

Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport heads north of the border this week as the team prepares to contest event six of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Knockhill (8/9 August).

The annual trip to the fan-favourite Scottish venue sees the team return to the 1.27-mile circuit in Fife, just north of Edinburgh. One of the shortest tracks on the BTCC calendar, Knockhill is also among the most demanding, with its narrow, undulating layout and unique character making it a favourite for both drivers and fans alike.

Following a hard-fought weekend at Thruxton, both Gordon Shedden and Árón Taylor-Smith will be aiming to bounce back and return to the sharp end of the grid after showing encouraging pace at the high-speed Hampshire circuit.

Home favourite and three-time BTCC champion Shedden boasts an impressive record at Knockhill, having claimed four race victories and 11 podium finishes at his home circuit during his illustrious career so far. The Scotsman will be hoping to add to that tally in front of his home crowd this weekend.

Alongside 'Flash', Irishman Taylor-Smith also has fond memories of the Fife venue. An Independents class winner at the venue in 2023, he has consistently scored strong points and will be looking to build on that record this weekend.

Heading into event six, Shedden sits ninth in the Drivers' Championship, with Taylor-Smith occupying 12th. Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport remains fifth in the Teams' Championship and third in the Independent Teams' Championship, with the team focused on closing the gap in both standings as the season enters its second half.

Following Saturday morning's opening 50-minute Free Practice session (10:30), the all-important Qualifying Groups (14:05) and 17-lap Qualifying Race (15:05) will determine the grid for Sunday's three races.


Sunday's races are scheduled for 11:15, 14:15 and 17:20, with all three contests broadcast live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer Network in North America and the BTCC YouTube channel anywhere else in the world.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said:

“Knockhill is a unique circuit that always throws up plenty of challenges, but it’s one I really enjoy. I can’t wait to get back out there and see what we are capable of this weekend.

“We’ve shown throughout the season that we have strong race pace, and if we can back that up with a solid qualifying performance on Saturday, we’ll give ourselves every chance of fighting at the front.


“I’ve had some good results here in the past, so the aim is to keep building our momentum, come away with some strong points, and continue moving in the right direction.”

Gordon Shedden (#52) said:


“I can’t wait to get out on track this weekend in front of the home crowd. Knockhill is always one of the highlights of the season for me. I’ve had plenty of success there over the years, and there’s nothing quite like bringing the BTCC to Scotland.

“Our race pace has been strong this season, with a win, Independent victories and podium finishes proving what we’re capable of. The key now is qualifying further up the grid because we know we have the pace to fight at the front.

“If we execute the weekend well and maximise every opportunity, I’m confident we can be in the mix for podiums and give the Scottish fans something to cheer about.”

Knockhill’s rollercoaster layout sets the stage for the next chapter of the 2026 title fight


The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship now heads to Knockhill this weekend (8/9 August), after three pulsating races at Thruxton launched the second half of the season in spectacular style.

Hampshire’s speedbowl saw Josh Cook (Speedworks Corolla Racing - Toyota), Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK - Ford) and Tom Ingram (Team VERTU - Hyundai) each claim victory.

It was Cook, the ‘King of Thruxton’, who immediately took to the fore last time out, setting a time in Qualifying only 0.018 seconds shy of the all-time record to start the ‘Race to Pole’ from the front. The Toyota Corolla GR Sport driver stayed true to his nickname in the Qualifying Race, leading from lights to flag to start race day with a clear view.

Sunday started in similar fashion, as Cook once again led from start to finish to extend his record number of triumphs at the circuit to 11, whilst becoming the eighth winner of 2026 in just 13 races. Sutton stalked the #66 throughout the race to come home second as Daniel Rowbottom (Cataclean Plato Racing - Mercedes) took the team’s maiden podium in the BTCC.


After coming close in the opening bout, the championship leader would make his presence felt in the second race of the day, immediately taking the lead from Cook on the first run up to the Club chicane. Eventually, Sutton would cross the line with a 9.305-second lead as Ingram was handed a ten-second time penalty for track-limits infringements, dropping him from second to fifth.

The final race of the UK’s premier motorsport championship’s return to action favoured Ingram differently than the two previous contests. Starting second in the reverse-grid race, the Team VERTU star would take the lead from polesitter James Dorlin (Restart Racing - Hyundai) before reaching the first braking point at Campbell. The reigning champion would go on to take victory as the field behind fought robustly, leaving Ingram out in front to score vital points in his championship challenge.

Across the grid, NAPA Racing UK continues to lead the Teams’ Championship, while Alliance Racing/Ford remains at the head of the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ standings. LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing also retains its advantage in the Independent Teams’ order.

Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi) continues to lead the Independent Drivers’ Championship, while James Dorlin now tops the Jack Sears Trophy standings by two points.

With the high-speed challenge of Thruxton now complete, the BTCC heads north to Knockhill. The undulating Scottish circuit promises another action-packed weekend as the second half of the 2026 campaign continues.

Conquering the Crests

One man knows Knockhill’s bumps, brows and blind crests better than any other driver on the grid, three-time champion Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport - Toyota).

The Scottish favourite has four victories at his home venue, with his most recent coming back in 2015. Now in his second season in Toyota machinery, the #52 will be one to watch in Fife.

Aiden Moffat (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing - Audi) is another fan favourite heading home after a difficult weekend in Hampshire. The man who holds the record as the championship’s youngest race starter will be looking for a repeat of his early season form that saw him lift silverware.

Another Scot heading homebound is Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing - Audi), who, up until the opening weekend of this season in new machinery, had his best result in the BTCC at Knockhill. Now two points adrift from the top of the Jack Sears Trophy lead, the #17 will be eager for another career-best in front of his home crowd.

The fourth and by no means least of the Scottish drivers is BTCC newcomer Lewis Gilbert (WSR - BMW). The three-time race starter heads to his second event in the championship after narrowly missing out on points on his debut weekend at Thruxton.

TV, Timetables and Tickets

Complementing the tin top racing will be a sensational line-up of support series, as the Porsche Sprint Challenge Great Britain, MINI CHALLENGE, Caterham 7 Championship UK and Scottish Legends Championship complete the schedule of exciting races.

BTCC will be wowing the crowds both trackside and at home, with Saturday's 'Race to Pole' and the earlier qualifying session being streamed live via ITV Sport's YouTube Channel from 1400, before ITV4's seven-and-a-half-hour race day broadcast gets underway at 1030 on Sunday.

Remember, continuing what started for the first time in the championship's history in 2025, the BTCC is being broadcast globally with every race being streamed live in 2026 via the BTCC YouTube Channel, whilst fans in North America can watch the action on the Racer Network. Look out for the races on Sunday starting at 1115, 1415 and 1720 (BST).

There's no place like being there of course, and fans can purchase tickets in advance or on the gate throughout the weekend – visit here for more details.

title.rendered: Pole, Victory and Podium for Speedworks Corolla Racing at Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: Speedworks Corolla Racing enjoyed one of its strongest weekends of...

content.rendered:
Speedworks Corolla Racing enjoyed one of its strongest weekends of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship season at Thruxton, with Josh Cook delivering a dominant display that included pole position, a race win and a podium finish, while Ryan Bensley made an encouraging BTCC debut with the Cheshire-based squad.

The UK's fastest circuit provided the perfect stage for the Toyota Corolla GR Sport to showcase its pace, with the team immediately establishing itself as the benchmark during Saturday's qualifying session.

Cook produced a sensational lap to secure pole position from title rival Tom Ingram (Team VERTU), underlining both his confidence around Thruxton and the outright performance of the Speedworks-run package.

Alongside him, Bensley enjoyed an encouraging first qualifying session for the team, securing 17th on the grid, making his competitive debut in the #7 and continuing to build experience in touring cars.

Cook converted the prime starting position into pole position during Saturday's Race to Pole encounter, successfully absorbing relentless pressure from both Ingram and Ash Sutton (NAPA Racing UK) throughout the contest. Rarely afforded a moment to relax, Cook produced a flawless drive to secure maximum points ahead of Sunday's opening race.

Unfortunately, Bensley's Race to Pole ended prematurely following contact, forcing an early retirement despite another encouraging display.

Sunday began in equally impressive fashion as the #66 once again demonstrated his race craft and composure to convert pole position into victory in race one.

Although Sutton remained firmly within striking distance throughout the race, Cook never faltered, controlling the pace superbly to secure the first victory of the weekend.

Bensley continued his learning process by bringing the Corolla home in 19th position after another competitive midfield performance.

Race two presented a fresh challenge, with significantly reduced boost available to Cook following his earlier success. The Bath-born driver would end the bout in third after being penalised for an incident involving Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK), dropping from second to the third step of the podium.

Bensley was once again involved in close midfield battles throughout the race, overcoming contact and continuing to gain valuable experience before finishing 19th, narrowly missing out on his maiden BTCC championship points.

The reverse-grid finale promised another opportunity for silverware. Cook made an excellent start and quickly established himself inside the leading group, looking well placed to challenge for another podium before contact at the final chicane ended his weekend early.

Bensley's weekend also ended prematurely after contact with Lewis Selby (NAPA Racing UK) caused his retirement just three laps into the final bout of the weekend.

Despite the disappointment of the closing encounter, Speedworks Corolla Racing leaves Hampshire with considerable encouragement. Pole position, triumphs in both the Race to Pole and race one, together with a further podium finish, represent the team's strongest points hauls of the season, while Bensley's pace and professionalism on his debut provide plenty of optimism heading into the remainder of the championship.

Christian Dick, Team Principal, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "Thruxton was a weekend that really demonstrated what this team is capable of. Josh was exceptional from the moment the weekend began. Fastest in Qualifying by that margin around a circuit like Thruxton is something very special, and to follow that with victories in both the Race to Pole and Race One was a fantastic reward for everyone's hard work."

"Naturally we're disappointed with how the final race unfolded because another podium - and potentially even more - looked within reach before the contact. Even so, the pace we showed throughout the weekend gives us enormous confidence heading into the next rounds."

"Ryan also deserves a huge amount of credit. Stepping into the BTCC midway through the season is never easy, but he integrated into the team brilliantly, showed genuine speed and approached the weekend with real maturity. The results don't quite tell the full story, and we're all excited to see how quickly he continues to develop."

Josh Cook, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "Overall, it's been a really satisfying weekend. To take pole position, win the Race to Pole and then convert that into another victory on Sunday is exactly what we set out to achieve."

"The team gave me a fantastic car all weekend and it was capable of fighting at the front in every session. It's obviously frustrating to lose second place in Race Two through the penalty and then have Race Three end the way it did because we were right back in the fight again."

"Even so, there are plenty of positives to take away. The pace of the Corolla was excellent, and we'll head to Knockhill feeling confident."

Ryan Bensley, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "It's been a huge learning weekend, but one I've really enjoyed. Joining a team midway through the season is never straightforward, but everyone at Speedworks made me feel welcome from the outset."

"Qualifying gave me confidence that the pace is there, and although the races didn't quite fall our way with the incidents we experienced, I learned something every time I went out on track."

"The Toyota felt stronger every session, and I'm already looking forward to Knockhill. I know there's much more to come once I build more experience with both the car and the championship."

excerpt.rendered: Mikey Doble remains the driver to beat in the Independents...

content.rendered:
Mikey Doble remains the driver to beat in the Independents Trophy after tallying his fourth win of the season at Thruxton (25/26 July) on what was a fast and furious weekend in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship.

Returning to action following the traditional mid-season break, the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing driver punched in an ultra-consistent performance to extend his advantage at the top of the Indy Drivers’ standings to 23 points.

Arriving at the Hampshire circuit having clocked valuable mileage in his Audi A3 Saloon during a recent test at Pembrey, the 27-year-old wasted no time in hitting the ground running on Saturday as he set the fourth fastest time in practice. 

Come the Qualifying Race later that afternoon, the two-time race winner found himself in the thick of the action as he went wheel-to-wheel with a number of drivers before taking the chequered flag in ninth place. 

Starting on the fifth row of the grid for the first of Sunday’s three races around the 2.36-mile circuit, the former Jack Sears Trophy winner went on to wow the crowds with a captivating battle with the Restart Racing Hyundai i30 N of James Dorlin. 

Getting the better of Dorlin in the opening exchanges, Doble then covered him off in the remaining laps with a wheel-perfect display that crucially secured him a fourth Independent win of the season. 

With the field so tightly bunched together, Doble spent the remaining two races in the midst of the midfield battle, clinching a brace of top tens. Crucially, these translated into second and fourth place finishes when it came to the Independents Trophy. 

In addition to extending his own lead in the Independents Drivers’ Championship over the course of the weekend, Doble also ensured that LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing remain out front in the Independents Teams’ too. 

Mikey Doble: “It’s been one of those weekend’s where we’ve ticked all the boxes in terms of scoring an Independent win and extending our lead in the championship, yet I’m leaving having wanted a little more.

“We had a really good two-day test at Pembrey and the work that we carried out there left me feeling pretty confident that we could win some races this weekend. Sadly that didn’t materialise as we didn’t quite have the balance we wanted in the car. 

“Saturday was strong, and that set us up for a solid Sunday where we chipped away. Getting that Independents win in race one was a great way to start the day and we then just tried to keep our nose clean and make as much progress as possible in the remaining two races.

“Obviously I’d have liked a little more results-wise but to come away having stretched our lead is something we can’t turn our nose up at. I’m unsure how we’ll fare at Knockhill but I know the team will pull out all the stops to ensure we have as strong a car as possible.”

Victories in Hampshire for Josh Cook, Ash Sutton and Tom Ingram

The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship blasted back into action following its mid-summer break with a stellar trio of races at Thruxton today (26 July).

A huge crowd descended on the Hampshire venue as 22 tin-top stars took on the fastest circuit in the UK for Rounds 13, 14 and 15 of this year’s campaign.

Josh Cook became the eighth different race winner of the season so far before title protagonists Ash Sutton and Tom Ingram added to their respective tallies.

Speedworks Corolla Racing’s Cook has long been hailed the ‘King of Thruxton’, having previously taken ten career BTCC victories around the 2.36-mile circuit, although he had been waiting since 2022 for a further success.

Sutton’s record-breaking start to the season continued in yet more exemplary fashion, maintaining his championship challenge with an impressive win and two second places.

Team VERTU’s Ingram claimed two top five finishes before a vital win in the finale, keeping Sutton within sight in the fight for the title.

Alliance Racing/Ford and NAPA Racing UK top both the Manufacturers’/Constructors’ and Teams’ tables.

Mikey Doble remains at the head of the Independent Drivers’ order, whilst LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing hold sway in the Indy Teams’ table.

A brilliant day for James Dorlin – with two top six finishes overall – elevated him to the summit of the Jack Sears Trophy standings.

The BTCC returns in two weeks’ time for its annual trip north of the border, at Knockhill on the 8/9 August.

Cook extends winning record at Thruxton

Speedworks Corolla Racing's Cook took victory in the Thruxton opener, extending his winning record at the Hampshire venue with 11 overall victories.

Having set the pace during Qualifying, before going on to win the 'Race to Pole' on Saturday afternoon, the #66 Toyota Corolla claimed a commanding lights-to-flag triumph.

It was far from easy, however, with four-time BTCC champion Sutton keeping Cook honest throughout the contest. Whilst their pace on-track looked comparable, a lack of boost available for the #116 Ford Focus Titanium meant that second place was just reward for the current standings’ leader.

There was more joy behind as Dan Rowbottom secured the first ever podium for Cataclean Plato Racing, with the Mercedes squad showing improved pace this weekend. The result also confirmed that each of the six marques have now scored at least one podium so far this season.

Rowbottom got a great start, as well as benefiting from an early scuffle between Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) and Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai), and the #32 Mercedes A35 Saloon slipped into third – a position he held until the finish.

Series returnee Senna Proctor – substituting for the unwell Sam Osborne this weekend – drove brilliantly to take fourth, fending off the attentions from former teammate Ingram in the #80 Team VERTU Hyundai.

Sutton surges to sixth triumph of 2026

NAPA Racing UK's Sutton stood victorious in Round 14, extending his championship lead in the process.

Sutton got the better of good friend and opening race winner Cook, when the latter’s Toyota ran wide in the opening exchanges nd the #116 Ford Focus nipped by.

The four-time champion kept the rest at bay while Speedworks Corolla Racing's Cook fell back into the clutches of Ingram (Team VERTU – Hyundai) and later Cammish (NAPA Racing UK – Ford) in the final laps.

The battle between Cook and Ingram intensified, gradually building to a critical moment through the final chicane as the two cars went side-by-side while completely on the limit.

In truth, neither car made the corner with Ingram getting the better of it, as Cook's #66 Toyota Corolla endured a half spin before continuing.

This left Cook in the grasp of Cammish's Ford Focus in the latter stages as the pair swapped positions twice, with the latter eventually gaining the position.

There was even better news for Cammish and Cook on the final tour when a ten second penalty was confirmed for Ingram following excessive track limit infringements, meaning the pair completed the podium.

Ingram takes top spot in Thruxton finale

Team VERTU's Ingram took the chequered flag in the Thruxton finale, as the 2025 Champion stood triumphant for the second time in his title defence campaign.

A robust early move past pole-sitter Dorlin was enough to secure the deal as the young talented Restart Racing Hyundai driver fought valiantly to keep a gaggle of contenders behind.

The NAPA Racing UK Ford pairing of Sutton and Cammish were next through, but both were unable to make inroads into Ingram's early advantage as the experienced trio settled in to secure the all-important podium positions.

Team VERTU's Ricky Collard drove brilliantly from 11th on the grid to take fourth after a number of eye-catching moves – ending an often-frustrating weekend on a high for the #11 Hyundai i30N driver.

Proctor rounded off a great day with another top five finish, having been thrown into the #18 Ford Focus Titanium race seat at the final minute.

Dorlin eventually came home sixth but undoubtedly proved to be one of the stars of the Thruxton event as he scooped yet more Independents' and Jack Sears Trophy honours.

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU's Tom Ingram took the chequered flag in Round...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU's Tom Ingram took the chequered flag in Round 15 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship at Thruxton, as the 2025 Champion stood triumphant for the second time in his title defence campaign.

An early robust move past pole-sitter James Dorlin was enough to secure the deal as the young talented Restart Racing driver fought valiantly to keep a gaggle of contenders behind.

The NAPA Racing UK pairing of Ash Sutton and Dan Cammish were next through but both were unable to make inroads into Ingram's early advantage as the experienced trio settled in to secure the all-important podium positions.

Team VERTU's Ricky Collard drove brilliantly from 11th on the grid to take fourth after a number of eye catching moves – ending an often frustrating weekend on a high for the #11 Hyundai i30N driver.

There was heartbreak for LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing's Aiden Moffat as he made up an incredible 12 places before a mechanical issue brought his Audi to a halt.

Senna Proctor rounded off a great day with another top five finish, having been thrown into the #18 Ford Focus Titanium seat at the final minute following Sam Osborne's illness.

Dorlin eventually came home sixth but undoubtedly proved to be one of the stars of the Thruxton event as he scooped yet more Independents' and Jack Sears Trophy honours.

There was a frenetic late fight for seventh, which initially seemed to be going the way of Cataclean Plato Racing's Dan Rowbottom, before he eventually wound up 11th.

When the dust settled on the scrap it was Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport's Gordon Shedden that had sealed the position down the inside of Rowbottom's Mercedes through turn one in the closing laps, and he was subsequently followed by Tom Chilton (Team VERTU), Dexter Patterson (Steel Seal with Power Maxed Racing) and Mikey Doble (LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing).

excerpt.rendered: Toyota star proves why he is the King of Thruxton...

content.rendered:
Toyota star proves why he is the King of Thruxton

Speedworks Corolla Racing’s Josh Cook claimed victory in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Qualifying Race earlier today (25 July), as the multiple race winner again proved his pace at Thruxton.

Cook has enjoyed no fewer than ten BTCC wins at the fastest circuit in the country, albeit with his most recent triumph coming back in 2022, but the Bath racer grabbed this latest success with both hands.

After topping the times in the earlier qualifying session, Cook controlled the ‘Race to Pole’ from start to finish, keeping Tom Ingram at bay as well as negotiating a Safety Car restart with complete composure.

Team VERTU’s Ingram got a good start as the reigning champion looked to out drag Cook’s #66 Toyota Corolla on the run down to the complex, before the #80 Hyundai settled into second.

In truth, Ingram went on to take a relatively lonely second place, but he will have been slightly frustrated to see title rival Ash Sutton in his mirrors.

Sutton again proved to be one the feistiest competitors in the contest as he disposed of Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing) and teammate Senna Proctor (NAPA Racing UK) with an opportunistic early move, before later going on to relinquish Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK) of third place.

Cammish held on to fourth from Proctor and the hard-charging Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport), as the three-time champion charged from 11th on the grid to claim sixth on-the-road – although the latter was demoted post-race after receiving a five second penalty.

Morgan had to settle for sixth after dropping down the order slightly, before eventually making his way back past Cataclean Plato Racing teammate Dan Rowbottom, when the latter had a wild moment through Church.

Mikey Doble endured a rather lacklustre encounter as he ended up ninth in the LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing Audi, whilst the Hyundai of Restart Racing’s James Dorlin rounded out the top ten.

The Saturday headlines, however, belonged to Cook, as he secured his first BTCC pole position in 700 days and will now look to reignite his championship campaign with a haul of silverware tomorrow.

Rounds 13, 14 and 15 of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship take place at Thruxton tomorrow with the action getting underway in the UK on ITV4 from 11:00, with the races also being beamed around the world on Racer TV (North America) and the BTCC YouTube Channel (Rest of the World).

Josh Cook, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: “That’s what we needed and it’s a good place to start for tomorrow. I’m pleased for the team with all the hard effort they’ve put in. They’ve just put in so much hard work and I’m glad we’ve managed to get the start of a good result for them – we now need to convert that on race day. The car was a beauty to drive. It was nice to go into a race run there, deal with the tyre degradation, manage the gap back to Tom (Ingram), and if there’s anything to learn ahead of tomorrow then I’m sure we will do.”

title.rendered: Team VERTU ready for Thruxton Thrills

excerpt.rendered: Team VERTU will hope to replicate the fine results it secured at...

content.rendered:
Team VERTU will hope to replicate the fine results it secured at Thruxton last season as the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship has burst back into life at the fastest circuit in the UK this weekend.

Reigning champion Tom Ingram is the best placed of the four Team VERTU drivers in the standings, with a triple podium at Oulton Park prior to the summer break having helped him to close the gap on rival Ash Sutton in the title race.

Currently sitting 48 points behind Sutton, Ingram will be chasing his fourth win at Thruxton and is bidding to take to the top step of the podium for the second season in succession.

His victory last season was the first for Team VERTU at the circuit, and helped kickstart his charge towards a second BTCC title, with a strong showing this time around being vital as he looks to defend his crown.

Ricky Collard arrives at Thruxton sitting fifth in the standings having secured a podium finish at each of the four meetings run to date this year.

Collard’s results so far at the wheel of the Hyundai i30 Fastback N have been particularly impressive given the late nature of his deal to join the team, and the fact that he was returning to front-wheel drive for the first time since 2023 - having since focused his career on sports cars.

As he continues to work on extending his programme with the team, Collard will look to add to his podium tally this weekend to maintain his championship position, with the ultimate goal being to try and secure a maiden BTCC victory.

Tom Chilton, the most experienced driver on the grid with nearly 550 BTCC starts to his name, goes into the weekend sitting in an unrepresentative twelfth place in the standings after a difficult campaign to date, with a single podium finish at Snetterton back in May.

Despite being a self-proclaimed fan of the UK’s fastest circuit, Chilton has yet to make it onto the top step of the podium at Thruxton - making it the only circuit on the schedule where he has failed to achieve that feat.

Keen to make up ground in the standings, Chilton will hope to secure three strong results from the weekend with a first win of 2026 being the target.

Nicolas Hamilton arrives at Thruxton buoyed by a solid points finish last time out at Oulton Park, where he ended the weekend with a strong twelfth place.

That followed on from an eleventh place finish at Brands Hatch earlier in the year and a points-scoring performance in the qualification race at Snetterton, where he also secured victory in the Jack Sears Trophy for the first time.

With confidence on a high, Hamilton heads for Thruxton looking to maintain the progress he has made since joining Team VERTU at the start of the season with further points being the aim.

Alongside pushing for strong results on track, EXCELR8 will also use the Thruxton meeting to launch a new competition alongside TeamSport Karting aimed at giving someone the chance to compete in the BTCC-supporting MINI CHALLENGE Trophy next season.

The competition, named FastTrack and being promoted on the car of Ricky Collard, is only open to novice drivers without a racing licence and will run across five stages, the first of which will see drivers complete a series of assessments at one of ten TeamSport Karting circuits around the UK.

Sunday’s three races - scheduled for 11:45, 14:40 and 17:30 - will then air live on both ITV4 and ITVX in the UK. 

Tom Chilton, #3 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Even though I’ve never managed to take a win at Thruxton, it remains one of my favourite circuits on the BTCC calendar as it’s so unique – there really is nowhere else like it.

“I think it’s fair to say that the season hasn’t gone the way I hoped so far, and I’ve certainly had more than my fair share of bad luck during the opening four rounds of the season. However, the fact that we topped qualifying and scored a podium finish at Snetterton shows we have the pace and it’s all about now trying to ensure that we show that across a full weekend.

“Three strong finishes are the aim and with the speed in the car, there is no reason why at least one of those can’t be on the podium.” 

Ricky Collard, #11 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton is my home circuit, although it isn’t one where I’ve actually raced much in the past, with this only being my sixth visit despite the fact that I did my first race back in 2012.

“It’s a really challenging circuit with little margin for error, and it’s one where you have to be brave if you want to maximise your results, so it should play to my strengths as a driver.

“I’m going there in confident mood given the results I’ve picked up so far this season, and considering how strong the Hyundai has been there in the past. It’s no secret that I really want to get onto the top step of the podium and claim my first BTCC win, and I think Thruxton will give me a great opportunity to do that.”

Nicolas Hamilton, #28 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “The summer break has given me the opportunity to reflect on how my season has gone so far, and I’m really pleased with the progress I’ve made. To score points at three of the four meetings and take a Jack Sears Trophy win is great and has given me a platform on which to build through the rest of the year.

“Thruxton is going to be a fresh challenge given how unique the circuit is, but I go into the weekend with the same approach I have taken through the opening rounds, which is to keep pushing myself to develop and improve.

“Every time I go out on track, I feel more and more comfortable in the car and with the support of the team behind me, I’m hoping to push for more points finishes and to challenge for the Jack Sears Trophy win.”

Tom Ingram, #80 Team VERTU Hyundai i30 Fastback N, said: “Thruxton was arguably our best weekend of the season last year with a win and two second places, so it’s a great place to now get our title challenge back underway after the summer break.

“Although we hadn’t tasted victory until last season, Thruxton is a circuit where we have traditionally gone well and which plays to the strengths of the Hyundai. A lot of people look at the layout and say it’s all about top speed but you also need a car that handles well, which is exactly what we have.

“It’s important that we maximise our results this weekend to try and reduce the gap to Ash in the standings, but we also have to remember that the early summer break means we haven’t even reached the half-way stage yet and there is a lot of racing still to come.”

title.rendered: Restart Racing hit the top with Goodyear medium tyre run

excerpt.rendered: Chris Smiley led home Restart Racing teammate James Dorlin in...

content.rendered:
Chris Smiley led home Restart Racing teammate James Dorlin in the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship Free Practice session at Thruxton, as the Hyundai duo made good use of the Goodyear medium tyre compound.

The BTCC’s official and longtime tyre supplier – Goodyear – has brought its medium compound to the fastest circuit in the country for the first time in its history, with the abrasive and high-speed nature of the layout ordinarily requiring the hardest compound.

The Qualifying Race and three Sunday races will all take place with the traditional hard tyre in use, but teams have been given the opportunity in practice – and for ten minutes during qualifying later today – to run the faster rubber.

It was Restart Racing that benefitted in particular as it showed the tyre to be potentially around three tenths faster than the chasing pack.

Smiley pipped Dorlin by just 0.093s while championship leader Ash Sutton was next in the order in the new-for-2026 Ford Focus Titanium.

Another new model – Audi A3 Saloon – was fourth as Donington Park race winner Mikey Doble produced a good lap in the #88 LKQ Euro Car Parts with Power Maxed Racing machine.

Thruxton specialist Josh Cook followed in the Speedworks Corolla Racing Toyota, as the Bath driver looks to add to his ten victories so far here in Hampshire.

Dan Cammish (NAPA Racing UK), Tom Ingram (Team VERTU), Adam Morgan (Cataclean Plato Racing) and Gordon Shedden (Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport) completed the top ten positions.

There was a notable absentee from the lineup with NAPA Racing UK’s Sam Osborne being taken ill on the eve of the weekend. He is being replaced by multiple race winner Senna Proctor, who will race the Ford Focus Titanium under his traditional #18.

Lewis Gilbert (WSR) made his BTCC debut during the session while series returnee Ryan Bensley completed his maiden run with Speedworks Corolla Racing.

As a reminder following the mid-summer break, the finishing order of Free Practice is now split into two groups, odd-finishing-numbers (Group 1) and even-finishing-numbers (Group 2), for a 15-minute qualifying session to set their fastest times.

The group with the fastest qualifying time will occupy the odd-numbered grid positions for the Qualifying Race, ordered by their respective qualifying times. The other group will occupy the even-numbered grid positions, also ordered by qualifying times.

15 minutes after the qualifying session for Group 2 has concluded, the standard grid procedure for a race start begins, and the pit lane opens. The finishing order of the shorter ten-lap ‘Race to Pole’ will determine the grid for the first of Sunday’s traditional trio of races.

Half-points are awarded for the Qualifying Race. There are no bonus points for leading a lap, the fastest lap, or for pole position for the Qualifying Race, whereas the bonus points for leading a lap and the fastest lap are still available on Sunday.

Qualifying and the Qualifying Race can be found LIVE on the ITV Sport YouTube Channel worldwide from 13:50 later today.

excerpt.rendered: The prototype PM Junior Championship car was unveiled in Hampshire...

content.rendered:
The prototype PM Junior Championship car was unveiled in Hampshire earlier today (25 July), as media and fans gathered outside the Thruxton Centre for a first look.

Adam Weaver, Team Owner of Power Maxed Racing, carried out the official unveiling in front of members of the TOCA paddock, including the likes of BTCC Chief Executive Alan Gow and four-time BTCC Champion Ash Sutton.

Adam Weaver, Team Owner of Power Maxed Racing, said:

Marking another significant milestone in the build-up to the inaugural 2027 season, the championship presented both the prototype race car and its M-Sport engine, giving prospective drivers, families, teams and fans a glimpse of Britain's newest junior racing series.

The PM Junior Championship prototype car – dubbed the PM1 – will be displayed in front of the Thruxton Centre throughout the weekend, where members of the championship team are on hand to answer questions and provide information on the series, including driver eligibility, technical specifications, running costs and the opportunities available for young drivers looking to take the next step in their motorsport careers. 

Designed for drivers aged 14-17, the PM Junior Championship has been created to provide a clear, professional and cost-controlled pathway into circuit racing. Competing on the support bill of the Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship, the series combines high-performance machinery with a controlled technical specification to deliver close, competitive racing while keeping costs manageable. 

The prototype on display features the core elements that will define the championship car, including an M-Sport developed engine, a Quaife sequential gearbox and differential package, and a Cosworth electronics system, all supplied by technical partners with extensive experience at the highest levels of motorsport. 

Visitors interested in learning more about the PM Junior Championship are encouraged to visit the display throughout the weekend, where the team will be available to discuss the championship, the car and the opportunities available to prospective drivers, teams and commercial partners. 

Looking ahead, preparations are also underway for the prototype to make its first public on-track demonstration during a Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship event later this season, giving fans the opportunity to see and hear the car in action ahead of the championship's debut in 2027.

content.rendered:
The 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship returns to action this weekend at the high-speed Thruxton Circuit, with Speedworks Corolla Racing looking to build on the encouraging performances shown before the summer break.

Following a productive first half of the season, the Cheshire-based squad arrives at one of the championship's fastest and most demanding venues determined to convert its evident pace into another strong haul of championship points.

The weekend also marks an exciting new chapter for the team, as Ryan Bensley makes his Speedworks Corolla Racing debut alongside multiple BTCC race winner Josh Cook.

Thruxton has long been regarded as one of Cook's strongest circuits. The Bath driver has enjoyed considerable success around the Hampshire venue throughout his BTCC career, earning the nickname "King of Thruxton" thanks to a series of memorable victories and front-running performances over recent seasons.

With the Toyota Corolla GR Sport continuing to demonstrate impressive race pace throughout 2026, Cook heads into the weekend full of confidence as he targets another strong points haul in front of what is expected to be another capacity crowd.

For Bensley, the weekend represents the fulfilment of another career milestone. Following his appointment during the championship's summer break, the talented driver will make his first competitive appearance for Speedworks Corolla Racing, having already impressed during previous BTCC outings.

While adapting to a new team, new engineers and a new car presents an understandable challenge, Bensley arrives with confidence after previously enjoying success at Thruxton, giving him valuable knowledge of one of Britain's quickest racing circuits.

The summer break has also provided valuable time for the team to regroup, analyse the opening half of the campaign and prepare for the busy run of races that now lies ahead.

With both drivers eager to get back behind the wheel and the entire team refreshed following the short break, anticipation is high as the second half of the 2026 season gets underway.

Christian Dick, Team Principal, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said:"It's great to finally be going racing again after the summer break. Everyone has worked incredibly hard behind the scenes over the last few weeks and there's a real sense of excitement throughout the team heading into Thruxton.

"Josh has always been exceptionally strong there and it's a circuit that really suits both his driving style and the characteristics of the Corolla. He's earned the reputation as the 'King of Thruxton' for good reason, and we're looking forward to seeing what we can achieve together this weekend.

"We're also delighted to welcome Ryan for his first race weekend with the team. He's settled in brilliantly already and we're all excited to see him out on track. There'll naturally be plenty to learn as he gets familiar with the car and the team, but we're confident he'll adapt quickly and show the pace we know he's capable of.

"The first half of the season demonstrated the potential of our package. Now it's about maintaining that momentum, continuing to improve and making the most of every opportunity over the remaining rounds."

Josh Cook, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "It's always special racing at Thruxton. I've enjoyed some fantastic moments there over the years and it's definitely one of the circuits I look forward to most on the calendar.

"The Corolla has shown strong pace this season and hopefully we can hit the ground running after the summer break. It's a circuit where confidence is everything, so we'll be looking to maximise every session and put ourselves in the mix from the outset."

Ryan Bensley, Driver, Speedworks Corolla Racing, said: "I genuinely can't wait to get started. Joining Speedworks Corolla Racing is a fantastic opportunity and everyone's made me feel incredibly welcome from day one.

"Thruxton is actually one of my favourite circuits and somewhere I've enjoyed success before, so to make my debut with the team there makes it even more special.

"There's obviously a lot to learn with a new team and a new car, but I'm looking forward to working closely with Josh and the engineers, building confidence throughout the weekend and hopefully putting it all together."

content.rendered:
Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport heads to Thruxton, Hampshire, this weekend for event five of the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship. With the summer break coming to an end, the team returns to action looking to continue its fight at the sharp end of both the overall and Independent championships.

Following the six-week summer break, Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport is well placed in both championship standings, sitting fifth in the Overall Teams’ Championship and third in the Independent Teams' Championship, just 16 points adrift of the lead after a strong start to the 2026 campaign.

The team has claimed two outright race victories this season, one of only two teams to have secured multiple race victories so far. Árón Taylor-Smith was responsible for the first, delivering a masterclass in challenging conditions at Brands Hatch to secure his first overall BTCC victory in more than a decade. Gordon Shedden then added to the team's tally with a scintillating race three victory at a sweltering Snetterton, further underlining the credentials of the three-time champion.

Despite the frustrations of the most recent round at Oulton Park, the MB Motorsport Corolla continued to demonstrate its pace. Taylor-Smith started the Qualifying Race from the front, with a storming qualifying performance on Saturday to set the fastest time of the weekend, losing out on pole position to a safety car restart penalty in the Race to Pole. The #52 would then convert that Saturday speed into an Independent race victory in the weekend's opening contest. Shedden also enjoyed a strong Sunday, recording a trio of points-scoring finishes as the team continued to demonstrate encouraging progress.

In the Drivers' Championship, Scotsman Gordon Shedden currently sits ninth, having already amassed three times as many points as he had at the same stage of the 2025 season. Taylor-Smith occupies eleventh, with his points tally already more than double what he had achieved by this point last year.

In the Independent Drivers' Championship, the pair sit fifth and seventh respectively as they look to strengthen their championship positions at Thruxton this weekend (25/26 July).

Thruxton has long been a happy hunting ground for Shedden, with "Flash" claiming an impressive seven victories and eleven podium finishes during his illustrious BTCC career. Taylor-Smith is also no stranger to success at the Hampshire circuit, having secured a hat-trick of top-three Independent finishes there in 2024.

Following the 50-minute practice session (Sat, 10:25), the all-important Qualifying Groups (Sat, 14:00) and Qualifying Race (Sat, 15:05) will set the grid for Sunday’s racing action.

Sunday’s races are scheduled for 11:45, 14:40 and 17:30, with all three races available to watch live on ITV4 and ITVX in the UK, Racer Network in North America, and the BTCC YouTube channel anywhere else in the world.

Árón Taylor-Smith (#50) said: "We head to Thruxton, which is one of my favourites, after the summer break with plenty of positives to build on from the first half of the season. Collecting my first BTCC win in more than a decade and heading the field in qualifying have undoubtedly been the highlights, but we've also shown on numerous occasions that we have the pace to challenge at the front of the field. Everyone at Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport has been working incredibly hard behind the scenes to ensure we're in the best possible position as we resume our 2026 campaign, and our aim is to carry the momentum we've built so far into the second half of the season."

"Thruxton is a circuit that demands not only the right car setup, but also complete commitment behind the wheel. It's a track I've enjoyed strong results at in the past, so I'm looking forward to getting back out there and carrying our momentum into the weekend. Hopefully we can put together three strong races, score some big points, and continue to demonstrate what this team is capable of."

Gordon Shedden (#52) said: ”It’s great to be back in action after some time away from the track. We’ve shown on several occasions what we’re capable of, with the victory at Snetterton being a particular highlight for me. Alongside that, we’ve collected Independent wins and podium finishes, and despite a few ups and downs, we’ve continued to make strong progress in both championships with the Corolla."

"Thruxton is a unique circuit where outright speed has to be balanced with tyre management, so getting the setup right will be absolutely crucial. It’s a track I’ve always enjoyed and one that holds plenty of great memories, so if we execute the weekend well, there’s every reason to believe we can come away with a strong haul of points."

Mark Blundell, Sporting Director at Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport, said: "The 2026 season has delivered plenty of highs and lows for everyone at Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport, but we head into the second half of the campaign in a strong position, firmly in contention in both championships. Árón and Gordon have both produced some outstanding performances, claiming a race victory apiece alongside a strong collection of Independent wins and podium finishes. As we head to Thruxton, our focus is on building on the momentum from the opening four rounds and returning to the fight for silverware following a challenging weekend at Oulton Park."

"Everyone at Laser Tools Racing with MB Motorsport has worked incredibly hard throughout the summer break to ensure we're ready to hit the ground running. Now it's about maintaining that focus, continuing to work as one team, and taking another step forward at Thruxton this weekend."

title.rendered: Expanded line-up for WSR as BTCC resumes at Thruxton

excerpt.rendered: WSR resume the challenge for the 2026 Kwik Fit British...

content.rendered:
WSR resume the challenge for the 2026 Kwik Fit British Touring Car Championship with an expanded three-car line-up as the UK’s leading series returns from its summer break at Thruxton this weekend (25/26 July).
 
Joining BTCC race winners Charles Rainford (#99) and Daryl De Leon (#2) for the rest of the season aboard a trio of BMW 330i M Sports will be Scottish newcomer Lewis Gilbert (#29), who is switching to touring car racing from single-seater racing.
 
The 18-time title winners hold second place in the overall and Independent Teams’ championships after a fast and consistent start to the season, the highlights of which have been two victories for Rainford and two podiums for De Leon.
 
The #99 car is fourth in the Drivers’ points table after victory at Oulton Park, which was the third of his BTCC career. The 28-year-old from Horsham now returns to a circuit where he was a race winner in Porsche Carrera Cup GB in 2023.
 
Team-mate De Leon holds second place in the Independents’ standings – only five points behind the leader – and sixth in the overall championship.
 
The Anglo-Filipino, who is based in Cambridgeshire, was the Jack Sears Trophy winner for the weekend at Thruxton last year as he surged towards securing the title later in the season.
 
22-year-old Gilbert, from Dalry, North Ayrshire, has never raced at Thruxton and had his first taste of the BMW 3 Series BTCC car with a one-day test at Snetterton a week before the Hampshire event.
 
The Scottish driver is a UK and European Champion in karting and is joining WSR half a season into his maiden season of car racing.
 
In total, the team has won there nine times in the BTCC and significantly sealed BMW’s 100th series victory in 2017, as well as double wins with the 3 Series in 2019 and 2024.

Charles Rainford, #99 driver, WSR, said: "The Summer break has come earlier than normal this year because of the World Cup, and our wins at Snetterton and Oulton Park feel like an awfully long time ago, but we’ve had a good chance to assess where we are and plan strategically for the rest of the season. Thruxton is unique in the BTCC because so much of it is high-speed and because we don’t have the variable of option tyres on race day. The BMW seems to have a mixed history at Thruxton, so it’s hard to know where we’ll shake out, but if we work to the very best of our ability, we should be somewhere in the mix."
 
Daryl De Leon, #2 driver, WSR, said: "The summer break’s been very busy, quick and brilliant! I'm just ready to get down to business now at Thruxton and to activate my yournameonabtcccar.com campaign. I’m sixth in the championship and second in the Independent Drivers’ points, so I’m going to continue pushing on to climb the standings. Thruxton is traditionally a front-wheel-drive track so we’ll definitely have to dig deep if we want the success with the BMW however, we know that’s what it will take so that will be our plan."
 
Lewis Gilbert, #29 driver, WSR, said: "Ever since I agreed to join WSR for the remaining six events of the year, I’ve been counting down the days to my debut. The BTCC is 100 per cent where I want to race and to finally be here, with a positive first test at Snetterton in the bag, feels great. Touring Cars is a totally new game for me so I know I have a lot to learn and I’m not setting any outlandish targets for the weekend, but having the experience of the WSR team around me is going to be a huge help. I can’t wait to get going at Thruxton."

title.rendered: 7-Eleven: Gordon Shedden
